Mariupol Old Jewish Cemetry

Jewish Cemetery · Mariupol, Ukraine

Mariupol's founding date for this cemetery is unknown, though its oldest tombstone dates to 1870. Jews numbered 111 in 1847 despite not being officially permitted to settle until 1859; a first synagogue (destroyed in WWI) was built in 1864. Population reached 5,013 (16%) by 1897, alongside an active Bund movement, though a 1905 pogrom killed 22 Jews. By the 1910s, the community maintained 4 synagogues, a hospital, 4 schools, a Talmud Torah, and a loan fund; a second pogrom struck in 1919. Under Soviet rule, a Yiddish elementary school and library opened; population peaked at 10,944 (5%) by 1939. After German forces arrived in October 1941, about 8,000 Jews were murdered within days. Postwar, the community rebuilt to about 3,400 (1%) by 1959, with renewed activity in the 1990s; the 2001 census recorded 1,176 Jews.
